messages:
Sam: FYI customer (ACME) opened a ticket — invoice shows ~40% fewer tokens than their dashboard for streaming calls. They attached client logs and a sample request id: req_0a7f9c2b.
Maya: Can you paste the raw SSE frames from the client? Need to see the final chunk / cancel sequence.
Sam: Pasting excerpt from customer logs:
```
> SSE: event: token_chunk
data: {tokens: 512, seq: 1}
> SSE: event: token_chunk
data: {tokens: 480, seq: 2}
> SSE: event: token_chunk
data: {tokens: 120, seq: 3}
> CLIENT: abort() called (XHR aborted)
> connection: closed by client
```
Maya: Customer says dashboard shows 1,112 tokens for this request, invoice shows 700.
Alex: Looking now — initial hypothesis: our metering emits final token counts on "finalize" after KV cache flush. If the client aborts before the flush completes, we currently don't emit the finalize event (we drop it). That would make invoice < dashboard. :thinking_face:
Jordan: That matches product/billing symptoms: dashboard streams live counts (we increment on generation), invoice aggregates finalized metering events. If finalize event is missing, invoice understates usage.
Alex: I repro locally: used their JS SDK, started streaming, then immediately did `controller.abort()`. On the runtime trace I see partial tokens in-memory (kv_cache.dirty=true) but no metering event. Sample trace: ```trace_id=tr_9b2, req=req_0a7f9c2b, cache_dirty=true, connection_closed=true, metering_emitted=false```
metering-bot: Found log entry: `WARN metering: finalize skipped for req=req_0a7f9c2b, reason=conn_closed_before_flush`
Jordan: Ok — so it's a server-side missed emission. Do we know how many requests this affects?
Alex: Quick grep across last 30 days: ~0.09% of streaming requests show `conn_closed_before_flush` with non-empty cache. For high-volume customers that can be sizable.
Maya: Customer is asking for workaround/ETA. Any short-term mitigation?
Alex: Short term we can advise SDK customers to avoid calling `abort()` and instead allow the final frame (or send an explicit final marker). But that's not ideal. We can also add a server-side toggle `flush_on_abort` that forces cache flush + emit metering even when client disconnects. Small change in runtime (emit before final connection tear-down). I can PR this today.
Jordan: From billing side, if invoices already closed we need to decide on credits. For affected customers we might need to issue a manual adjustment. I'll need a list of affected req ids and dollar delta.
Sam: I'll ask the customer for sample req ids and timeframe and let them know we have an internal mitigation patch planned. Offering a temporary credit if delta > $250.
Alex: Implementation notes: modify stream tear-down path to run `flush_kv_cache()` synchronously before dropping connection; ensure idempotent metering emission to avoid double-counts. Also add unit test for abort path. I expect a PR + CI in ~24-48hrs, QA + deploy to canary in 48-72hrs.
metering-bot: Suggested patch check: ensure `metering_idempotency_key` uses request id + abort_count to dedupe emissions.
Jordan: If we emit on abort we might make invoices slightly higher than dashboard for some edge cases (if dashboard already counted the same tokens earlier). Need to ensure we don't double-bill.
Alex: Agreed — dedupe is required. Proposed rule: emit metering event on any terminal path if we haven't already emitted finalize for that req_id. If dashboard had already counted live tokens, invoice should match.
Maya: I'll draft the customer response: short summary, workaround (don't abort), ETA for server fix (48-72h), offer to follow up on credits.
Sam: Assigning action items: Alex -> PR for flush_on_abort + dedupe, Jordan -> prepare billing impact analysis, Maya -> customer comms.
Alex: Opening PR now (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234) — will update when CI passes.
Sam: Thanks — keep this thread updated.
Maya: tagging @Jordan for billing review once PR lands. :eyes:
